required_stages.description: Allocate a fresh flat (BATCH*M*N,) (or (BATCH, M, N)) output of A's dtype inside run().

One logical pass with no global-memory intermediate (no split-K partials, no repacked operand; the output tiles may be spread over several launches): each (batch, M-tile, N-tile) output tile accumulates the full K range sequentially into a local fp32 accumulator via a tensor-core product, with zero-filled edge loads and clipped/masked stores; cast to A's dtype at the store.

forbidden_substitutions.message: A library GEMM replaces the whole computation.
The @ operator on tensors is a library GEMM.
Host-side transpose/repack or copy of an operand: forbidden under the provisional no-repack rule (open review item); in-kernel tile transposes are fine.
Cross-call caching keyed on input tensors is forbidden.
Atomic accumulation suggests split-K, which is a different reduction structure.
Possible downcast of fp32 operands below TF32 precision.
No zero-filled scratch is part of this operator; only an uninitialised output is expected.

required_evidence.message: No matrix-multiply primitive found; the GEMM must use a tensor-core product.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned flat (BATCH*M*N,) tensor (or flat view of a fresh (BATCH, M, N) buffer) must be allocated inside run() and must not share storage with A or B

timing_boundary.notes: The GPU time of all device work launched by run() is counted (here only the GEMM launch(es)); zero-copy views, host descriptor/metadata construction and the output allocation call are host-side work and not GPU time. Provisional rule (open review item): no transposed/packed copy of A or B and no cross-call cache of input-derived data; if a repack is ever permitted it must be device work inside run() on every call, where its GPU time is counted.
